authority: Owner directions in this development task

decisions.decision: ai-governance-regime is the organizational wrapper around the RealityEngine, aligned with the global standards and frameworks the package's documents track (ISO/IEC 42001/42005/42006, NIST AI RMF and AI 600-1, the EU AI Act, OWASP Agentic Top 10, MITRE ATLAS and the others in SPECIFICATION.md section 2).
constraints: Alignment claims need a pinned source per framework before any machine cites it.

decisions.decision: This domain is the proof of workflow for new domain production: each factory step is carried out and recorded here, so the next domain can follow it.
constraints: Record each step's inputs, outputs and verification in PACKAGE_STATUS.md as it is done.

decisions.decision: The package follows the ifrs-accounting factory layout.
constraints: Directories appear when their step produces content; none is created empty.

decisions.decision: The canonical machines are the 17 base machines M-GOV-01..17 from SPECIFICATION.md 4.3 and HARDENING_TRANSITION_RULES.md. The governed target domain travels in the asset frame; the intake corpora's per-domain copies are not carried over.
constraints: The intake corpora stay in intake/ as received.

decisions.decision: Each machine has its own regions in the governance band (input <= 16 cells, an 8-element output); the PE composes the lifecycle and gate signals into each input, and a fixture aggregator (GOV00) folds the verdicts onto the four domain verdict elements.
constraints: The specification's cell numbers become signal provenance (inputSemantics), not regions.
The band is proposed as [16960:17429]; allocation follows the admission workflow (GOV-R04).
Corrected 2026-11-25: [16960:17439] was the 0.1.0 band; the 0.2.0 machines use [16960:17429] (PACKAGE_STATUS.md, 0.2.0 record).

decisions.decision: Before anything else changes, the machines conform to schemas/machine.schema.json and carry the CESs (one regular expression each) that represent the specified behaviors.
constraints: Checked by tools/verify_machines.py with the repository's own schema, pattern and cloneable gates.

decisions.decision: Every agentic workflow (W1-W7) and every Source in governance-sources.json is in v1 of the domain.
constraints: A Source whose producer does not exist yet is built, not dropped; until it exists its machines are tested only against interned sequences.
The hooks into approve-domain.sh, deployments and cut-release.sh are changes to those repositories, approved separately.

decisions.decision: Agent behavior is generated runtime-neutral (schemas/agent-behavior.schema.json) and rendered per runtime, so the move from OpenClaw to ACP-hosted agents changes an adapter, not the agents.
constraints: localOpenClawStack machine-behaviors/runtimes renders OpenClaw and ACP; the committed OpenClaw agents stay byte-identical.

decisions.decision: The scope stays the 18 machines GOV00-GOV17 (GOV-SD-04 reaffirmed). The received hardening workplan's 315-machine corpus, its [16960:17087] band and its fixed cells 16987-16991 are source material, not targets.
constraints: M-GOV-15/16/17 in RESOLUTION_WORKPLAN.md are GOV15/16/17 here (corpus-315's M-GOV-HRD-313..315).
Cells 16987-16991 survive only as inputSemantics provenance labels (GOV-SD-05).
The workplan's 1,867-machine and p99 <= 820 ns figures are designed, not measured (GOV-R09).

decisions.decision: Threat classification and dynamic, reactive threat observability are a separate peer domain, threat-dynamics, not part of ai-governance-regime. This domain focuses on closing the seven wrapper gaps (GAP_ANALYSIS.md).
constraints: The NIST SP 2400-102 adversarial-ML taxonomy (NISTAML attack classes, agentic .061-.067) is threat-dynamics' specification, not this domain's.
Control identifiers for this domain come from the governance frameworks pinned under GOV-R07, not from SP 2400-102.

decisions.decision: Observe vs decide: threat-dynamics owns classification, detection, red-team harnesses and vendor canaries, and publishes the results as Sources; ai-governance-regime consumes them only as gate inputs and owns the decision.
constraints: The two domains couple only through published lanes, declared on both sides (governance-sources.json producerDomain; threat-dynamics' published-lane contract).
The Sources produced by threat-dynamics: gate_redteam_pass (GOV01, gap 3), mon_canary_drift_score (GOV16, gap 6) and mon_xdomain_mu_agg (GOV16, gap 5).
Admission order: threat-dynamics, the producer, is admitted before this domain.

decisions.decision: One shared extension corpus and regression profile carries both peer domains above the corpus vector budget (16944), as MACHINE_CONCEPT.md 9.3 provides. The standard vector budget does not change.
constraints: The 8-bit watchdogs GOV07, GOV08, GOV09, GOV12, GOV14 and GOV16 reach the parity gate through this extension corpus (closes GOV-R11).
threat-dynamics is allocated next to this domain's band, below the clone space (20480).

independentReview: Domain review and the admission workflow (scripts/approve-domain.sh) remain required.
